findings.title: Engineered yield depends on a sustaining water system
findings.claim: The focus's possible gift and possible ruin can be read within one productive system: yield depends on water, enclosure, cultivation, and retaining ground.
findings.mechanism: The focus occurrences carrying productive yield, the tree-covered garden, and the slippery exposed surface meet pericope occurrences for produce, crops, palms, grapevines, flowing water, sinking water, trellises, collapse, and growing wealth; the contacts turn the final surface into the failure point of the conditions that made the garden productive.
findings.reader_payoff: The reading distinguishes loss of visible fruit from loss of the water, supports, boundaries, and ground that made fruitfulness possible.
findings.containment: The literal hope for a better garden and warning of a slippery bare surface remain intact. No particular weather object, engineering history, or exclusive systems metaphor is asserted.

epistemic.reason: A trusted channel nomination is landed on exact supplied focus and context occurrences; the systems synthesis remains a bounded secondary relation.
